I have some old Dichromate gelatin that I am storing inside a plastic bottle. I will dispose of it when it is full, however I was thinking…..

Would it be better to expose the gelatin to the sun for a couple of hours? I read something at my kid’s library that CRVI is bad for the environment while CRIV or CRV was better (sorry I’m not 100% sure on which state was best). I thought maybe it was something us DCG folks can do and make Al Gore happy at the same time, or was he all global warning? 

Thanks,

Tony

posts.author: DJ Mathson
posts.content_md:
Yes, dichromates are toxic and a hazard to the environment, especially to aquatic organisms. You can use Sodium Metabisulfite to convert CrVI to CrIII, but maybe you have to get the dichromate into a solution first.

See holowiki at the middle and the end of this page:

[http://www.holowiki.com/index.php/G307_DCG_Formula](http://www.holowiki.com/index.php/G307_DCG_Formula)

posts.author: JohnFP
posts.content_md: Another technique, if you are using fixer, is to pour all unused, scraped and excess emulsion into one of your empty distilled water jugs. Then as you use up your fixer (it is blue) pour the used fixer in the gallon jug with the AmDi. You should instantly see the orange turn to blue. When it is blue it is in the CrIII state. I have always had enough fixer to nuetralize all my excess AmDi.
